flags: The company obtained control over EugenLight Technologies in January 2026.
In 2024 the company completed the acquisition of 100% shareholdings of ASEPCAYMAN and CHE.
GAPT's acquisition of a 16.48% shareholding of Hong Kong United Ascend Holdings Limited was completed in September 2024.
share_unit_note: filed shares 4,429,553,000 against 2,207,573,526 quoted (x0.498); values are per quoted share

business_model.claim: ASE sells outsourced semiconductor manufacturing services, mainly assembly (packaging) and testing.
quotes: ASEH is a leading provider of semiconductor manufacturing services in assembly and testing.

business_model.claim: Its offering covers packaging, interconnect materials, engineering testing, wafer probing, final testing and EMS for computing, communications, industrial, automotive and server applications.
quotes: Our services include semiconductor packaging, production of interconnect materials, front-end engineering testing, wafer probing, and final testing services, as well as integrated solutions for EMS in relation to computing, peripherals, communications, industrial, automotive, and server applications.

business_model.claim: The company works in every stage of chip manufacturing except circuit design and wafer fabrication, so it sits downstream of foundries.
quotes: We are involved in all stages of the semiconductor manufacturing process except circuit design and wafer fabrication.

business_model.claim: EMS is supplied through the USI Group subsidiary. Smaller revenue also comes from a real estate business and integrated circuit manufacturing.
quotes: We offer a broad range of semiconductor packaging and testing services, and we offer EMS through USI Group.
In addition, we have been generating revenues from our real estate business and the manufacturing of integrated circuits.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 as management belief
business_model.claim: The customers are semiconductor companies that outsource manufacturing, including fabless firms and IDMs.
quotes: We believe that the growth in the number and scale of fabless semiconductor companies that rely solely on independent manufacturers will continue to drive our growth.

Similarly, the availability of technologically advanced independent manufacturing services has encouraged IDMs, traditionally reliant on in-house manufacturing, to increasingly outsource their manufacturing requirements to independent semiconductor manufacturing companies.

business_model.claim: The company names its strategic alliance with TSMC as one of its competitive strengths.
quotes: our long-term relationships with providers of complementary semiconductor manufacturing services, including our strategic alliance with TSMC.

business_model.claim: Most sales go to customers headquartered outside Taiwan: export sales were NT$529,419.5 million, or 82.0% of 2025 sales, compared with 85.0% in 2024.
quotes: Revenues from our export sales, based on the country in which the customer is headquartered, were NT$506,134.7 million and NT$529,419.5 million (US$16,876.6 million) in 2024 and 2025, respectively, which contributed 85.0% and 82.0% of our total sales for those years.

business_model.claim: The reporting segments are packaging, testing, EMS and other. In 2025, packaging revenue was 308,342.6 (47.8%), testing 71,900.2 (11.1%) and EMS 257,192.7 (39.9%), in a table stated in NT$ millions.
quotes: goodwill is allocated to the cash-generating units for evaluation of impairment: packaging segment, testing segment, EMS segment and other segment.

business_model.basis: stated in P2 segment table and text
business_model.claim: Margins differ sharply by segment: 2025 gross margin was 22.1% for packaging, 31.0% for testing and 9.2% for EMS.
quotes: Gross margin is calculated by dividing gross profit by their respective operating revenues.
Our gross margin for EMS business increased to 9.2% in 2025 from 8.9% in 2024.

business_model.claim: Most prices and revenues are in U.S. dollars, so NT dollar/US dollar movements affect both reported revenue and costs.
quotes: The majority of our prices and revenues is denominated in U.S. dollars.
Any significant fluctuation in exchange rates, especially between NT dollars and U.S. dollars, will affect our costs and, in turn, our revenues.

business_model.claim: In packaging, customers usually supply the silicon die on consignment, so its cost is usually left out of both revenue and cost.
quotes: In the case of semiconductor packaging, the cost of the silicon die, typically the most costly component of the packaged semiconductor, is usually not reflected in our costs (or revenues) since it is generally supplied by our customers on a consignment basis.

business_model.claim: Prices for a given technology tend to fall over time. Shifting the mix toward more complex packages and tests partly offsets this.
quotes: The semiconductor industry is characterized by a general trend toward declining prices for products and services of a given technology over time.
Declines in average selling prices have been partially offset by changes in our revenue mix, and typically the selling price is largely dependent on the complexity of the services.

business_model.claim: Fixed costs are high, especially in testing, so capacity utilization drives gross margin.
quotes: Our operations, in particular our testing operations, are characterized by relatively high fixed costs.

Increases or decreases in our capacity utilization rates could have a significant effect on gross margins since the unit cost of our products and/or services generally decreases as fixed costs are allocated over a larger number of units.

business_model.claim: Depreciation, amortization and rental expense in operating costs rose to 9.6% of revenue in 2025 from 9.1% in 2024, mainly because of higher capital expenditure.
quotes: In 2024 and 2025, our depreciation, amortization, and rental expenses included in operating costs as a percentage of operating revenues was 9.1% and 9.6%, respectively.
The increase in depreciation, amortization, and rental expenses as a percentage of operating revenues in 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily a result of increased capital expenditures.

business_model.basis: stated in F3; the link to future depreciation is inferred from P2
business_model.claim: Cash paid for property, plant and equipment was 164,642,502 in 2025 against 79,521,938 in 2024, in a table stated in thousands of NT$.
quotes: Payments for property, plant and equipment

business_model.claim: Raw materials are the largest cost and are concentrated in EMS: they equalled 78.7% of EMS revenue in 2025, and 48.4% of total revenue, down from 51.5% in 2024.
quotes: In 2025, raw material costs accounted for 78.7% of our operating revenues from EMS, and our revenues generated from EMS contributed to 39.9% of our operating revenues.
In 2024 and 2025, raw material cost as a percentage of our operating revenues was 51.5% and 48.4%, respectively.

business_model.claim: Gold wire remains a principal packaging material, and the company says gold prices will keep affecting its raw material costs.
quotes: Thus, we expect our raw material costs to continue to be affected by fluctuations in the price of gold.

business_model.claim: Labor cost rose to NT$73,128.2 million in 2025 from NT$64,267.7 million, driven by higher headcount, especially in packaging.
quotes: Labor costs in 2025 were NT$73,128.2 million (US$2,331.2 million) compared to NT$64,267.7 million in 2024, primarily due to higher employee headcount, especially in our packaging business.

business_model.claim: R&D spending rose to 5.1% of revenue in 2025 from 4.8%, tied to demand for leading-edge advanced packaging.
quotes: Research and development expenses as a percentage of our operating revenues was 5.1% in 2025 compared to 4.8% in 2024.

business_model.claim: Revenue grew 8.4% to NT$645,387.7 million in 2025, driven by packaging and testing.
quotes: Operating revenues increased by 8.4% to NT$645,387.7 million (US$20,573.4 million) in 2025 from NT$595,409.6 million in 2024, primarily due to higher sales in our packaging and testing business.
The increase in packaging and testing revenues was primarily driven by growing demand in our leading-edge advanced packing services and testing business.

business_model.claim: EMS revenue fell 5.2% in 2025 because communication and automotive products recovered slowly.
quotes: Revenues from our EMS business decreased by 5.2% to NT$257,192.7 million (US$8,198.7 million) in 2025 from NT$271,293.3 million in 2024, primarily due to the slow recovery of general communication and automotive products.

business_model.claim: Gross margin rose to 17.7% in 2025 from 16.3% on a richer packaging and testing mix and higher utilization. The stronger NT dollar and higher utility costs partly offset the gain.
quotes: Our gross profit as a percentage of operating revenues, or gross margin, was 17.7% in 2025 compared to 16.3% in 2024, which was primarily as a result of higher packaging and testing revenue mix and higher factory utilization of our packaging and testing equipment, offset in part by the appreciating NT dollars and higher utility costs.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, F3 and P2
business_model.claim: Borrowing costs are a growing expense line. Long-term borrowings rose to 202,612,796 from 121,750,192, and finance costs to 7,503,269 from 6,777,032 (tables in thousands of NT$).
quotes: The changes in net non-operating income and expenses were primarily due to a decrease in gain on our foreign exchange hedging activities and an increase in finance costs.

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal: the first quarter has historically been lower than the preceding fourth quarter because of holidays.
quotes: In general, our first quarter operating revenues have historically decreased over the preceding fourth quarter, primarily due to the combined effects of holidays in the U.S., Taiwan, and elsewhere in Asia.

business_model.claim: In 3Q26, packaging, testing, EMS and others made up about 50%, 11%, 38% and 1% of revenue.
quotes: Net revenues from packaging operations, testing operations, EMS operations, and others represented approximately 50%, 11%, 38%, and 1% of the total net revenues for the quarter, respectively.

Gross margin increased by 3.3 percentage points to 30.6% in 3Q26 from 27.3% in 2Q26.

quotes: announces its unaudited consolidated net revenues for October 2026.
